question: A dashboard must show the progress of a 2-minute import to the user who started it. The client never sends data while it waits. Which transport fits best?
options: WebSockets with a custom message protocol
WebTransport datagrams
Server-Sent Events: one-way, plain HTTP, automatic reconnection
Short polling every 100 ms
explanation: Progress is server-to-client only. SSE delivers it with less code and fewer operational concerns than WebSockets; polling every 100 ms wastes requests.

question: A chat app runs on 3 instances behind a load balancer. Messages sent by users on instance 1 are not seen by users connected to instance 2. What is missing?
options: A pub/sub layer (Redis pub/sub, NATS, a broker) so every instance receives each message and forwards it to its local sockets
Sticky sessions
HTTP/2
A bigger instance so everyone connects to the same one
explanation: Each instance only knows its own connections. Fan-out through a shared channel is required as soon as there is more than one instance.

question: SSE connections drop exactly every 60 seconds in production but not locally. What is the likely cause and fix?
options: SSE has a 60-second protocol limit; switch to WebSockets
The load balancer closes idle connections after 60 s; send a heartbeat comment (for example every 15 s) and keep client reconnection enabled
Node.js closes responses after 60 s by default and it cannot be changed
The browser limits SSE to one minute
explanation: Proxies and load balancers have idle timeouts. Heartbeats keep the connection active; the same applies to WebSockets (ping/pong).

question: A generated WebSocket client connects to `wss://api.example.com/socket?token=eyJhbGciOi...`. What is the concern?
options: None, query strings are encrypted by TLS so they are safe everywhere
WebSockets do not support query strings
Tokens must be sent as a binary frame
URLs are written to proxy and server access logs and browser history; prefer a cookie or a short-lived token sent in the first message
explanation: TLS protects the token on the wire, but URLs are logged in many places. Browsers cannot set an Authorization header on WebSocket, so use cookies or an initial auth message.

question: Your product needs presence and live updates for 200 000 concurrent users worldwide, and real time is not your core business. What deserves serious consideration?
options: A managed real-time service (Ably, Pusher, Supabase Realtime, Firebase) instead of running the connection layer yourself
Short polling every second from every client
One very large Node.js instance
Long polling with sticky sessions
explanation: Hundreds of thousands of global connections bring capacity, fan-out and edge concerns. A managed service turns that into a bill instead of a project; compare cost and lock-in.
